blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — insulin glargine pharmacokinetic profile
stem: A client asks what clinicians mean when insulin glargine is described as having “no pronounced peak.” Which explanation is most accurate?

options.A: It is absorbed slowly, producing a relatively constant 24-hour serum concentration/time profile without a pronounced peak compared with NPH insulin.
options.B: It produces an early sharp serum concentration peak followed by rapid decline, with basal insulin activity generally ending within a few hours after injection.
options.C: Its prolonged basal profile depends on mixing it with rapid-acting insulin before injection so the combined preparation releases insulin more evenly throughout the day.
options.D: It has minimal glucose-lowering activity during the first day after injection, with the basal effect beginning only after several consecutive daily doses.

rationale: Current LANTUS prescribing information states that after subcutaneous injection, insulin glargine shows slower, more prolonged absorption and a relatively constant concentration/time profile over 24 hours with no pronounced peak compared with NPH insulin. The label also notes that the time course of insulin action can vary between patients and within the same patient, so the 24-hour profile should not be interpreted as an identical duration in every individual. Therefore A is correct. B describes the opposite pharmacokinetic pattern, C conflicts with the instruction not to mix LANTUS with other insulins, and D incorrectly states that meaningful glucose-lowering activity is delayed until repeated dosing.
educational_objective: Explain that insulin glargine's “no pronounced peak” refers to slower, prolonged absorption with a relatively constant concentration/time profile over 24 hours compared with NPH insulin, while recognizing that insulin action varies among individuals.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine) / FDA labeling
source_document_title: LANTUS (insulin glargine) injection — Full Prescribing Information

source_claim_supported: After subcutaneous injection, insulin glargine has slower, prolonged absorption and a relatively constant concentration/time profile over 24 hours without a pronounced peak compared with NPH insulin; insulin action can vary between and within individuals.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12/PDF p.16: educate client about medications; review pertinent data prior to medication administration; evaluate client response to medication.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices as substantive pharmacokinetic or administration explanations without the original absolute-word distractor cues.
Qualified the 24-hour statement as a concentration/time profile rather than a universal exact duration and balanced option lengths while retaining one label-supported explanation.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches current LANTUS pharmacokinetic labeling. The wording avoids converting the observed 24-hour concentration profile into a guaranteed individual duration, and the correct option is not the longest choice; B–D remain plausible but clearly incorrect alternatives without a second defensible answer.
